identity.real_world_identity_notes: Final development of the Lotus 49, the Ford Cosworth DFV-engined car pressed back into service after the Lotus 63 proved unsuccessful, racing until 1971. It used a Hewland-Lotus five-speed manual gearbox.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift.

The standard gate was read from the cockpit by watching the lever and the driver's hand through a shift rather than from a gate plate, which these cars do not have. The same method read three dogleg gates in dataset 0.3.28 that registered sources then corroborated, so it distinguishes the two gates rather than defaulting to one.

The gearbox is a racing Hewland, engaged by dog rings rather than synchronisers, so the driver must match revs on a downshift for the gear to engage cleanly. The downshift blip is therefore required, not optional.

The dog-ring construction is inferred from Hewland's design approach rather than stated by a reviewed source. A source showing this gearbox was synchronised would change the gearbox type and make the downshift blip optional.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.lotus-49c.20260814t054846492z-6f53d533 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the 49C and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

Wikipedia states a Hewland-Lotus 5-speed manual gearbox, and the live drive selected five H-pattern gears. Dog-ring engagement is Hewland's design approach rather than a stated property of this gearbox, so it is an inference from the make and is recorded as such.

The registered source names a Hewland-Lotus five-speed manual but does not state how it engages. Dog-ring construction is inferred from Hewland's design approach rather than stated by a reviewed source, so this value is medium confidence: a source showing the gearbox was synchronised would change it, and would make the downshift blip optional.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Hewland-Lotus five-speed - rev-match every downshift. The dog rings are inferred from Hewland's design approach rather than stated by a source, so one showing this gearbox was synchronised would make the blip optional.
